title: drop SP deletes an active sprint whose items are all dropped, bypassing close's ops row and worker cleanup
goal: Found by the SP-m3azo2y7 review of BG-j7f3dlop: sprint_leftovers and cmd_drop (_tools/bl_items.py) never read the sprint's status, though kb/_self/backlog.md says drop is for a sprint that has not run; an active sprint whose items are all dropped and whose review story is todo is deleted by drop, which skips close's record_close ops row and the work/<id> worktree and branch cleanup. drop of a sprint that has started refuses and names close; a planned sprint drops as now.

run: import sys;t=open('_tools/bl_items.py',encoding='utf-8').read();s=t[t.index('def sprint_leftovers'):t.index('def cmd_drop')];sys.exit(0 if 'active' in s or 'planned' in s else 1)

repro_reason: the defect needs a started sprint in a scratch git repo with workers' leftovers; the text check pins that the leftover rule reads the sprint's status
notes: Merged from ST-5sgru6ls “A planted test proves drop of a sprint takes its research and review stories and refuses while a live or claimed item remains” at the 2026-10-12 draft triage: both come from the SP-m3azo2y7 review and change cmd_drop/sprint_leftovers (_tools/bl_items.py). Its planned suite test (tests.py -k drop_sprint in the land e2e test file) is out under the test policy D-2tq4fhgs, which deleted that file: the fix is proven by its repro and by a drop run on a planned sprint in a temporary git repository (check errors=0, and the refusals on a non-dropped item and on a claimed story).
